"Risk of Rain Returns: A Triumph in Timeless Chaos"

Rating: ★★★★★

"Risk of Rain Returns" is a glorious resurrection of the classic roguelike that stole our hearts, delivering an adrenaline-pumping experience that blends nostalgia with innovation. Developed by a team clearly passionate about the original, this sequel exceeds expectations and redefines the standards for the genre.

The first thing that strikes players is the stunning visual upgrade. The pixel art is more vibrant and detailed than ever, breathing new life into the familiar landscapes while preserving the essence of the original game. Each level feels like a handcrafted masterpiece, with a meticulous attention to detail that adds layers of immersion.

The heart of "Risk of Rain Returns" lies in its chaotic gameplay, which has been elevated to new heights. The addition of new characters with unique abilities introduces a fresh layer of strategy to the mix, making each run feel distinct. The synergy between items and characters creates an addictive loop of experimentation, ensuring that no two playthroughs are ever the same.

The soundtrack, a hallmark of the series, returns with a bang. The music seamlessly integrates with the intense action, enhancing the atmosphere and contributing to the overall sense of urgency. It's a symphony that fuels the player's determination to survive against all odds.

One of the standout features of "Risk of Rain Returns" is its commitment to cooperative play. The multiplayer experience has been refined, allowing friends to join forces and face the ever-intensifying challenges together. The camaraderie and shared victories amplify the fun factor, making this game a must-play for social gamers.

The procedurally generated levels maintain the unpredictable nature of the original, keeping players on their toes as they adapt to the constantly shifting environments. This dynamic element ensures that even veterans of the series will find themselves surprised and delighted by the evolving challenges that lie ahead.

"Risk of Rain Returns" is more than just a sequel; it's a love letter to the fans who have supported the franchise over the years. It successfully captures the essence of what made the original great while introducing new elements that push the boundaries of the roguelike genre. In a gaming landscape filled with fleeting trends, "Risk of Rain Returns" stands as a testament to the enduring appeal of well-crafted, challenging gameplay. Strap in, gather your friends, and get ready for a wild ride that will keep you coming back for more.

It's nice because you can adjust damage taken/dealt, but if you want to play normally it's not playable at higher difficulty. Attacks are not easier to avoid due to the game being 2D, but they are more telegraphed, so it is more manageable with certain abilities.

Risk Of Rain Returns takes everything that made the original game the phenomenal roguelike that it was, and improves almost everything. Enhanced graphics/spritework, New items, characters, artifacts, stages, etc. New single-player challenges in the Providence Trials, which are (mostly) all fun and replayable to try for Gold rank.

As an ongoing fan of the Risk of Rain franchise, it's safe to say I really enjoy this game! There is just a few issues I would like to address but apart from them, this game was very well done. The issues I will address will be listed down below:

Issue #1 - Risk of... what rain?

As you all are aware the title of the game implies there is rain, but yet I rarely see any rain during any of the game play. Kind of contradictory no?

Issue #2 - Too political

Time in and time out when playing the games you can notice that some of the elite versions of the enemies are blue and red. This is clearly a nod to the democratic and republican party respectfully and I am just tired of seeing my beloved games get involved with political issues.

Issue #3 - Not enough genitalia

Risk of Rain 1.5:
New Characters (some returning from RoR2) 
New Enemies from RoR2 redone in RoR1 style 
Updated sprites for everything. 

Probably going to be the last good RoR made now that Gearbox owns the IP outright and already have a Gacha style mobile RoR game in the works that's going to be loaded to the brim with microtransactions.

Has some benefits over Risk of Rain 2, namely that it no longer feels like you're either winning spectacularly or already dead, and the overall fidelity of the assets has obviously improved over the original Risk of Rain release, but there's not a whole lot past that I can say I like.

This franchise as a whole feels like what happens when you get a decent, engaging idea going, but the team developing it lacks experience. Every entry in it thus far has had several things I could point to bringing it down. It usually manages to be fun despite this, but the potential available is decidedly not being met.

In Risk of Rain 1, the primary let-down was the controls being bad, the maps being far too large, and mobility feeling about nonexistant. As far as a first game goes, however, this is highly forgiveable.

In Risk of Rain 2, the maps are [i]still[/i] too large, the terrain is very plain, and you will more often than not end up winning hard until something spontaneously one-taps you without you even knowing what it is. Not to mention a final boss that is entirely obnoxious to fight. Still, movement was a lot better, as was the aiming and controls generally.

But then we get here, to Risk of Rain Returns. The controls are still much better - I'll give it that. I'm still very annoyed I can't aim with the mouse properly, but that's coming in a future update, so I'll let it slide. But the rest of the problems are still here in force. Sure, you can move while shooting now, that's great, but you're still slower than molasses in January, so I still feel like a slug in tar. The maps are still immense and irritating to navigate, and both of these issues compound the difficulty unnecessarily.

But the thing I hate most about this release is the Providence Trials. I don't know what was going through the heads of those that made them, but the vast majority of them are ridiculously infuriating to complete. Difficulty out the nose, with several of them utilizing gimmicks that the game was very clearly not designed to handle. I [i]loathed[/i] them, and while you can ignore them for alternate skill unlocks (as other unlock methods are available), there are several items that can [i]only[/i] be obtained via them, and I find it obscene.

And yet honestly, despite this all, this review could've been a tentative positive one. Indeed, for a while, it [i]was.[/i] But the constant difficulty imbued in so many of the challenges in combination with the entirely unnecessary put-down lines thrown at you every time you lose is just barely enough to tip it over the edge into the negative, as I can't respect developers who feel the need to insult their own players.

Overall, Risk of Rain as a whole has been defined to me by its inherent possibility for greatness in combination with its consistent ability to disappoint and fall short of that promise. It's decent, and you'll probably have fun, but it [b]will[/b] be very rough around the edges.
